subject: Interactive lab ops: benchmark orchestration & test-harness check
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@nimble.ai>, Rachel Park <rachel.park@nimble.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Interactive lab ops: benchmark orchestration & test-harness check

Hi Alex / Rachel —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. To keep momentum, we propose splitting the engagement into two focused sessions this week:

1) POC kickoff & prompt walk-through (90 min, interactive) — prompt set review, routing choices, canary plan
2) Load & benchmarking lab (120 min) — controlled throughput ramp, latency SLO verification, test-harness run-through

Suggested windows (PST):
- Tue 14 Dec, 10:00–11:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Wed 15 Dec, 09:00–10:30 or 13:00–14:30

Before we lock times, a couple of asks so we can size the run:
- Throughput target (requests/sec) and expected avg prompt+context token length
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95 targets) you care about
- Will you provide a canonical prompt corpus or should we use the sample prompts (attached) as a staging set?
- Any egress/firewall IPs we should know for VPC whitelisting?

I've attached a short runbook and our load-harness config to show how we emulate traffic and measure KV/cache effects. Marcus and Grace are on the thread for routing/batch policy questions.

Attachment: redwood-runbook-v1.pdf (5 pages)
Attachment: load-harness-config.yaml

If those windows work, I’ll send calendar invites and a shared Drive folder with artifacts.

Thanks,
—Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@nimble.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Park <rachel.park@nimble.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interactive lab ops: benchmark orchestration & test-harness check

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the clear plan. We can do the kickoff on Tue 14 Dec 14:00–15:30 PST and the load lab on Wed 15 Dec 13:00–15:00 PST (extend the 120 min slot by 30 if needed).

A few details from our side:
- Primary throughput target: ~1,500 requests/sec (we'd like to validate sustained throughput and a 30-min soak).
- Latency SLO: p95 under 180 ms end-to-end (includes our client overhead), p50 ideally < 60 ms.
- Avg token profile: prompt+context ~ 80 tokens, expected generation avg 40 tokens.
- We'll provide a 2k-row sample prompt CSV (attached) but can expand if you need more variety.
- Network: our infra team needs the list of source IPs to whitelist. I will send their contact separately.

Question: can Redwood simulate 200 concurrent sessions with prefix caching enabled and also run a baseline without caching? We want to compare per-token cost & latency delta.

Attached: nimble-sample-prompts.csv

Looking forward — Alex
Alex Soto
Head of Platform, Nimble AI
alex.soto@nimble.ai | +1 (650) 555-0220

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Soto <alex.soto@nimble.ai>, Rachel Park <rachel.park@nimble.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2027 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interactive lab ops: benchmark orchestration & test-harness check

Good notes Alex — yes, we can run both cache-enabled and cache-disabled profiles in the same window. Operational notes for the lab:

- Routing: we'll route traffic to a quantized 8-bit variant for cost comparison, and keep an FP16 job as fallback. We need to know the expected sequence-length distribution (Alex's token numbers are helpful).
- Concurrency: our harness simulates concurrent sessions; 200 concurrent sessions with 1,500 rps implies a short inter-request spacing — we'll coordinate a ramp plan (start at 10% and step up every 10 minutes).
- Metrics: we'll emit p50/p90/p95 latency, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. Please confirm if you also want tail-latency histograms at 99th.
- Pre-stage: to exercise KV cache behavior we recommend a 15–20 minute warmup phase where we replay common prefixes; please point us to any prompt prefixes you expect to be reused.

I've attached an updated harness config with the ramp template and a quick checklist for the lab (network whitelist, dataset link, and a recommended ramp schedule).

Attachment: load-harness-config.yaml

If everything looks good I'll finalize the event invites and the Drive folder.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Rachel Park <rachel.park@nimble.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interactive lab ops: benchmark orchestration & test-harness check

Thanks team — the proposed slots work for us. Quick items from our ops & procurement folks:

- Firewall: our network team will whitelist the Redwood egress IP block. Contact: Peter Liu (peter.liu@nimble.ai). They need the CIDR list by EOD today if possible.

Thanks — I’ll look out for the calendar invites.

Great — all set. I've booked the two sessions and shared the Drive folder with final artifacts: runbook, harness config, and the sample prompts you provided. Calendar invites below: please accept when you can.

- Kickoff: Tue 14 Dec 14:00–15:30 PST — https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123def456ghi
- Load lab: Wed 15 Dec 13:00–15:00 PST — https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=lab789jkl012mno

Final runbook highlights (attached):
- Agenda: kickoff (prompt review, routing decisions, canary plan); lab (warmup, stepped ramp, soak, post-mortem)
- Ramp: 0% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% over 60 minutes, then 30-min soak at target
- Fallback: auto-failover to FP16 variant if error rate > 1.5% for 2 consecutive minutes; explicit manual rollback path documented
- Deliverables: latency/cost dashboard, raw harness traces (CSV), and a short exec summary

Attachments: redwood-runbook-v1.pdf, load-harness-config.yaml
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the sessions.
